title: Inside the Gemini factory: Accelerating partner solutions
raw_text: With the new unified Gemini experience, enterprises can bring third-party partner capabilities directly in Gemini through standardized connectors (spanning Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A) runtimes, and REST APIs), alongside emerging declarative skills and plugins. For independent software vendors (ISVs), this unified architecture unlocks a powerful opportunity to embed domain-specialized intelligence, regulated workflows, and live systems of record directly into enterprises' daily workflows. Yet turning a compelling use case into an enterprise-ready integration often stalls in engineering friction, from choosing the right extensibility primitive and wiring authentication to orchestrating multi-step tool execution and rendering inline interactive experiences. To eliminate these bottlenecks, Google Cloud launched the Gemini factory—an intensive co-innovation initiative designed to help enterprise software partners go from a blank whiteboard to agentic solutions listed on Google Cloud Marketplace in record time. Through hands-on workshops in global technology hubs—including San Francisco, New York City, Sunnyvale, London, Paris, Tel Aviv, and Tokyo—Google Cloud specialists work side-by-side with partner teams to ideate, architect, and build the next generation of enterprise AI solutions with Gemini. Specifically, the Gemini factory helps partners: Choose the right agentic architecture across MCP connectors, skills, plugins, and autonomous agents. Go from an initial use case to a production integration in days rather than months. Accelerate customer activation with funding incentives and go-to-market (GTM) support. Let’s dive in and see how we make all of that a reality. Choosing the right architecture: agents, MCPs, skills, and plugins In previous iterations of enterprise AI, third-party integrations often operated as isolated top-level agents, forcing employees to leave their workflow. When software providers arrive at the Gemini factory, they evaluate how their capabilities plug into Gemini across four complementary architectural primitives rather than competing extremes: Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors: The foundational data and tool pipe for exposing external APIs, search, and CRUD operations to Gemini as callable tools registered in Agent Registry in Gemini platform. Declarative Skills ( .md ): Open Markdown configurations stored in Skills Registry that equip Gemini with domain-specific instructions, operational guardrails, and repeatable multi-step workflows across connectors. Plugins: The composite packaging and governance primitive in Gemini and Google Cloud Marketplace that bundles one or more Connectors and Skills into a single turnkey solution for IT administrators to govern and Gemini users to invoke. AI agents (A2A): For enterprise ISVs whose value lies in proprietary algorithms, regulated workflows, or strict compliance rules, standalone A2A agents run in an isolated partner environment while plugging into Gemini as callable connectors—keeping intellectual property protected, guaranteeing deterministic execution sequences, and maintaining tamper-proof audit trails. Rather than forcing developers into a single mold, Gemini unifies all four primitives into a coherent enterprise fabric—passing shared session context into partner connectors and chaining outputs across the enterprise ecosystem. Technical velocity: From use case to production Once the right architectural pattern is defined, the Gemini factory compresses months of integration work into a streamlined, AI-assisted engineering pipeline that brings partner development teams and Google Cloud experts together side-by-side. Accelerated Partner Development Pipeline This execution velocity is powered by three core capabilities in Gemini platform: Antigravity & AI-assisted builder workflows: Rather than writing boilerplate from scratch, developers build and govern solutions in Antigravity, an AI-first development environment. Using pre-built Rapid Agent Development (RAD) skills and AI-assisted workflows, partner teams rapidly translate use-case specifications into working architectures, scaffold remote MCP connectors or agent runtimes, author declarative .md skills, and run automated pre-ingestion validation harnesses. Flexible backend primitives (MCP, skills, plugins, and ADK): For most integrations, teams expose platform APIs via a hosting-agnostic Remote MCP Connector (on Cloud Run or their existing cloud) and layer on declarative Skills ( .md ) bundled into a turnkey Plugin . When a use case requires closed-IP models or strict deterministic execution, partners use the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) and the A2A protocol to expose their runtime as a callable connector in Agent Registry. Inline adaptive experiences (native MCP apps): Instead of redirecting users to fragmented external portals or maintaining complex custom UIs, Gemini keeps users in the flow of work. Through native MCP apps and guided inline components, partner integrations dynamically stream rich, context-aware visual canvases directly in Gemini while chaining outputs across Google Workspace and other enterprise connectors. From working prototype to marketplace distribution The Gemini factory is structured as an end-to-end commercial runway, not just a hackathon: Stage Program pillar Partner benefit 1. Build Seed credits Offset upfront costs: Upfront scoped credits to offset build and porting costs, consumption-based performance credits as partners scale, and scoped engineering support to accelerate development. 2. Launch Cloud marketplace Enable discoverability: Publish directly to Google Cloud Marketplace with streamlined billing, procurement, and enterprise integration to gain direct visibility across global enterprise and mid-market accounts. 3. Scale Co-marketing & GTM Amplify market demand: Access custom co-marketing and launch assets, social promotion, PR kits, launch spotlight campaigns, and Google-funded campaign packages for top-performing partners. Enterprise deployment architecture: Regardless of whether a partner builds a Skill, Plugin, MCP server, or A2A agent, the architecture is designed to keep customer onboarding frictionless and partner IP secure. Gemini users access the partner integration in Gemini using native OAuth, Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), and streamlined Bring Your Own License (BYOL) flows, while the partner maintains backend security, data sources, and proprietary tooling within their own project perimeter. Built-in discoverability: Partner solutions are published directly to Google Cloud Marketplace and featured in AI Solution Finder , giving enterprise customers a central place to discover validated MCP connectors, plugins, and agents today—and making it simple for IT administrators to configure and govern them in Gemini. Comprehensive incentives & go-to-market: Google Cloud supports verified partners through every growth stage. Qualified solutions unlock Seed Credits upon Marketplace publishing and performance credits to offset operational inference costs, paired with GTM assets and sales enablement to turn engineering milestones into a net-new pipeline. Featured partners: proven speed to impact Recent Gemini factory (previously referred to as the Agent Factory) cohorts have already brought a wave of industry-specific agents to life. Here is how nine software partners took complex enterprise challenges and deployed production-grade solutions built with Gemini in days: Aily Labs Aily Decision Intelligence Agent The Aily Decision Intelligence Agent unifies 360° enterprise performance metrics to deliver predictive business diagnostics and actionable strategic recommendations. Built for executive decision-makers, it interrogates complex operational and financial datasets to forecast performance trends, identify supply disruptions, and guide strategic resource allocation through an intuitive, mobile-first interface. “Our mission is to bring real-time, AI-powered decision intelligence to every business executive. The Agent Factory workshop was an incredible catalyst; it enabled our team to wire up complex predictive reasoning models into the Gemini Enterprise runtime, activating Aily Super Agent in record time; orchestrating thousands of specialized agents, connecting insights across multiple business domains, and presenting them through a single, intuitive interface for the user. Having side-by-side engineering support helped us prove out high-impact executive scenarios and accelerate our roadmap toward a verified listing on Google Cloud Marketplace.” — Reynaldo Espana, VP of Engineering, Aily Labs FlowX Capital Markets Document Reconciliation Agent FlowX's Capital Markets Document Reconciliation Agent streamlines high-stakes financial operations, including institutional document extraction, multi-party reconciliation, and loan pack completeness audits. Leveraging specialized document intelligence and Kubernetes-backed agent runtimes, it cross-checks disparate contracts, regulatory filings, and credit documentation to flag discrepancies in real time, drastically reducing cycle times for back-office operations. “In capital markets and lending, precision, auditability, and data security are non-negotiable. What impressed us most about the Agent Factory was how rapidly we could implement complex business validation rules and multi-source document ingestion without compromising on enterprise compliance. Transitioning from raw use cases to a functional prototype in a single workshop demonstrated the sheer execution velocity possible on Gemini.” — Serban Chiricescu, Founder & Chief Technology Officer, FlowX.AI Klarvant Digital Governance Analyst Agent The Analyst Agent by Klarvant provides outside-in discovery and analysis of an enterprise’s external namespace: post-quantum readiness, certificate and TLS hygiene, email security, supply-chain risk, and external exposure. It tracks post-quantum migration endpoint by endpoint, matches supplier and dependency events to the points where they touch the estate, and answers plain-language questions with audit-ready evidence and custom dashboards built on request. “What Gemini does exceptionally well is reason over complex technical evidence and explain it in plain language. That is exactly what governance needs. A board member or even a CISO does not want a list of ciphers; they want to know whether the company is ready and what to do next. With the Agent Factory, Gemini became the bridge between our intelligence and the people accountable for it.” — Endre Fehn, Chief Technology Officer, Klarvant NextLM AI Prospecting Agent The NextLM AI Prospecting Agent brings tenant-native prospect intelligence into Gemini. Powered by the Savant model family, it ranks the B2B accounts and buyers most likely to convert using behavioral data across 300M+ companies, 370M+ professionals, and 1.3B+ tracked news articles. Each customer gets an isolated model that is further trained on its own closed-won and closed-lost data, so prioritization reflects what actually wins for that business. Built to work alongside other agents in Gemini, it hands ranked accounts and buyer context to research, outreach, and CRM connectors, turning “who should we pursue and why now” into action across the workflow. “Building autonomous B2B sales agents requires blending live external market signals with deep enterprise CRM context. The Agent Factory eliminated the typical development friction—our engineers used the RAD framework to go from an initial architecture diagram to an active, working prospecting agent in under 24 hours. The hands-on co-engineering with Google Cloud gave us the confidence and tooling to bring a production-ready solution straight into the Gemini Enterprise ecosystem.” — Chris Anzalone, Founder & CEO, NextLM Optimizely Mark Marketing Calendar Deck Builder Agent Optimizely Mark Marketing Calendar Deck Builder Agent converts cross-functional marketing strategies, campaign timelines, and experimentation roadmaps into executive-ready slide decks and visual briefs. Grounded in campaign performance metrics and content repository data, it enables marketing leaders to generate unified omnichannel schedules, align global teams, and track milestone delivery in seconds. “Marketing teams spend countless hours manually consolidating disjointed campaign plans and roadmaps into presentations for leadership. The Agent Factory allowed us to harness Gemini and Vertex AI Vector Search to turn that manual chore into an autonomous, one-click experience. In just one intensive day, our team built an agent that unlocks immediate productivity gains for enterprise marketers and seamlessly plugs into our broader Mark platform.” — Kevin Li, SVP Product, Optimizely Ping Identity PingID Device Management Agent Employees manage their own MFA devices just by asking. When someone gets a new phone, the agent displays a live PingID pairing QR code with real-time status directly in Gemini, rendered with A2UI. Employees can also list, rename, set a default, or remove devices without opening a portal or filing a help desk ticket. That replaces a help desk call, and the over-the-phone identity check that social engineering attacks exploit, with a short conversation. “Every new phone and every last day at work is an identity event, and too many of them still turn into help desk tickets. Working side by side with Google Cloud in the Agent Factory, we built agents that let employees manage their own MFA devices and let admins resolve identity requests in one conversation. With ADK, A2A, and A2UI, those experiences run natively in Gemini, and every action stays scoped to the user, confirmed by a person, and accountable.” — Loren Russon, SVP, Product & Technology, Ping Identity Sinch Sinch RCS Messaging Agent The Sinch RCS Messaging Agent enables enterprises to create and manage RCS business agents, draft interactive messaging campaigns directly from natural-language prompts, execute rich RCS broadcasts, and monitor delivery reports, built with Gemini and Sinch's carrier infrastructure. “Collaborating with the Agent Factory team dramatically accelerated our timeline from prototype to a verified listing on Google Cloud Marketplace. Leveraging their structured environment and pre-built RAD skills, our engineering team was able to rapidly assemble, secure, and validate a complete lifecycle agent for RCS, covering enterprise authentication, RCS agent provisioning, prompt-based campaign drafting, and real-time delivery reporting. We walked away with a production-ready solution that harnesses Google Cloud’s ecosystem to help businesses deliver richer, more interactive conversational experiences at scale.” — Antoine Sein, Senior Engineering Manager, Developer Experience & Agent Experience, Sinch THG Ingenuity Shopping Assistant Insights Agent Shopping Assistant Insights converts shopper conversations into actionable commercial insights and plain-business answers grounded in BigQuery analytics. It tracks shopper demand, assistant performance, and customer friction while maintaining strict data privacy. title: BigQuery measures is now GA: Unifying BI metrics and knowledge graphs for AI accuracy
raw_text:
To answer a complex business question, an AI agent must understand two things: what happened, and why . The what is a governed metric, like revenue at risk; the why is the network of relationships that produced it. Because metric definitions, a.k.a. measures, traditionally live in business intelligence (BI) platforms while relationships live in knowledge graphs, an AI agent only ever sees half the picture. It guesses the rest, leading to confident but sometimes wrong answers. To solve this hallucination problem, we introduced measures in BigQuery , which are now generally available. Historically, organizations needing both BI and knowledge graphs had to run two siloed technology stacks: one to calculate reliable metrics, the other to map out entity relationships. Bridging them entailed brittle data pipelines and runtime reconciliation by analysts and AI agents, who held the connections in their heads or in sprawling prompts. This patchwork approach wasn't just slow and expensive — it’s where data governance broke down, as every analyst and prompt may define joins and metrics differently. Figure 1: A unified model for defining BI metrics and knowledge graphs in one place, for powering AI agents, SQL, GQL and dashboards. To replace manual reconciliation, you need a single model that understands both the structure of your business and the math that measures it. BigQuery measures builds directly on BigQuery Graph to deliver that unified foundation. By defining measures directly on the graph entities they describe, your BI dashboards and AI agents don't just get a number they can trust — they get the relational context behind it. Finally, they can reliably answer both the what and the why . "With BigQuery measures, we can now deliver self-documenting data products. Defining measures natively in BigQuery ensures Looker Dashboards, Conversational Agents and our Data team queries operate on identical logic, guaranteeing metric alignment across leadership and significantly reducing data team maintenance overhead." - Amanda Reelick, Head of Data Enablement, Woolworths NZ One model to answer both the what and the why Let's walk through an example. Suppose your retail bank's risk analytics team spots a sudden spike in transaction activity in the Prague district. You need to know whether this represents healthy customer growth or concentrated risk exposure. Answering requires two pieces of evidence: how much money actually moved (the what ), and which specific accounts it flowed through (the why ). At most banks, getting that answer takes two teams, two tools, and two numbers that are rarely reconciled. With BigQuery, your underlying data is already in place — whether in native tables or in a borderless Lakehouse . With a single schema, you can define a semantic model directly over your existing transaction, account, and district tables — with no data movement and no secondary system: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '-- Entities, relationships, and measures, declared in one model
CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH retail_banking.BankingGraph
 NODE TABLES (
 retail_banking.trans AS Trans
 KEY (trans_id)
 PROPERTIES (
 trans_id, account_id, amount,
 MEASURE(SUM(amount)) AS total_trans_amount
 ),
 retail_banking.account AS Account
 KEY (account_id)
 PROPERTIES (
 account_id, district_id, stmt_frq,
 MEASURE(COUNT(account_id)) AS account_count
 ),
 retail_banking.district AS District
 KEY (district_id)
 PROPERTIES (district_id, city, state)
 )
 EDGE TABLES (
 retail_banking.trans AS POSTED_TO
 KEY (trans_id)
 SOURCE KEY (trans_id) REFERENCES Trans (trans_id)
 DESTINATION KEY (account_id) REFERENCES Account (account_id)
 NO PROPERTIES,
 retail_banking.account AS LOCATED_IN
 KEY (account_id)
 SOURCE KEY (account_id) REFERENCES Account (account_id)
 DESTINATION KEY (district_id) REFERENCES District (district_id)
 NO PROPERTIES
 );'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2d550>)])]> To determine whether the Prague spike reflects broad growth or concentrated exposure, your team checks whether the transaction volume is spread across many accounts or driven by just a few. Using GRAPH_EXPAND , you flatten the graph and roll up both measures with the AGG() function: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '-- Volume by city, and the accounts behind it, each counted once
SELECT
 District_city,
 AGG(Trans_total_trans_amount) AS total_volume,
 AGG(Account_account_count) AS accounts_involved
FROM GRAPH_EXPAND("retail_banking.BankingGraph")
GROUP BY District_city;'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2e090>)])]> You can ensure accurate reporting by using measures that have been “grain-locked” — where a fixed level of granularity has been assigned to how facts and dimensions are modeled. Because a single account can have thousands of transactions, joining the two tables can duplicate account rows. A standard SQL COUNT(account_id) would overcount those accounts, leaving your risk and finance teams with conflicting numbers. BigQuery measures preserve the native grain of each entity, counting every account only once regardless of how the tables are joined. The second half of the investigation is about connectivity: Which accounts are driving the Prague activity? You can answer that with a traversal in GQL (the ISO-standard Graph Query Language) over the exact same model: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "-- Which accounts moved money in Prague
GRAPH retail_banking.BankingGraph
MATCH (:Trans)-[:POSTED_TO]->(a:Account)-[:LOCATED_IN]->(d:District)
WHERE d.city = 'Prague'
RETURN DISTINCT a.account_id"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2fb50>)])]> Neither query requires a separate system, and both evaluate against the same governed definitions. New features in BigQuery measures While the preview introduced grain-locked measures tightly integrated with BigQuery Graph, real-world production analytics demand more than basic sums — and enterprise AI agents need programmatic ways to discover and interpret those metrics. The GA of BigQuery measures focuses on two key areas: richer modeling and visualization for complex business logic, and native semantic discovery for the agentic ecosystem. Richer modeling, querying and BI visualization To enable more expressive and flexible measure definitions, MEASURE() supports both composite expressions and derived measures; this capability is GA. Rather than repeating conditional logic across queries, you can define baseline aggregates once and compose them into higher-order calculations on the same table using AGG() . BigQuery validates these formula dependencies at schema compilation time to catch circular references or invalid aggregations early. Downstream dashboards and AI agents can then query complex ratios and net metrics at any dimensionality with consistent accuracy. For example, on your Trans node, you can define settled volume alongside total volume, and then derive unsettled volume and unsettled percentage directly from those building blocks: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '-- Compose custom calculations, conditional expressions, and derived ratios
PROPERTIES (
 trans_id, account_id, amount, fee, is_settled,
 MEASURE(SUM(amount)) AS total_trans_amount,
 MEASURE(SUM(CASE WHEN is_settled = TRUE THEN amount ELSE 0.0 END))
 AS settled_volume,
 MEASURE(AVG(CASE WHEN amount > 10000 THEN amount ELSE NULL END))
 AS avg_large_trans,
 -- Derived: written in terms of the measures above
 MEASURE(AGG(total_trans_amount) - AGG(settled_volume)) AS unsettled_volume,
 MEASURE(
 SAFE_DIVIDE(AGG(total_trans_amount) - AGG(settled_volume),
 NULLIF(AGG(total_trans_amount), 0)) * 100.0
 ) AS unsettled_pct
)'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2e890>)])]> Query across multiple fact tables Enterprise data models routinely span multiple business processes. Joining separate fact tables that share a common dimension — such as transactions and credit cards linked to the same bank account — traditionally causes a "chasm trap," where cross-fact multiplication inflates both metrics. The new start_node argument in GRAPH_EXPAND solves this by isolating each fact table into its own expansion tree. BigQuery evaluates each measure at its native grain before joining the results on the shared entity: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '-- Transactions and cards per account, each evaluated at its own root grain
SELECT
 ET.Account_account_id,
 AGG(ET.Trans_settled_volume) AS settled_volume,
 AGG(EC.Card_card_count) AS total_cards_issued
FROM
 GRAPH_EXPAND("retail_banking.BankingGraph", start_node => "Trans") AS ET
LEFT JOIN
 GRAPH_EXPAND("retail_banking.BankingGraph", start_node => "Card") AS EC
ON ET.Account_account_id = EC.Account_account_id
GROUP BY ET.Account_account_id;'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2d350>)])]> By expanding each fact table from its own root ( Trans and Card ), each branch maintains its exact grain — even for accounts with transactions but no issued cards. Visualize in Data Studio With the updated BigQuery connector in Data Studio , you can now connect directly to BigQuery graphs and build interactive visualizations powered by native measures. Data Studio honors the aggregation logic defined in your graph model, keeping complex calculations consistent across charts while preventing accidental client-side re-aggregations. Built for the agentic era Attach business meaning to your measures In a large enterprise schema, it’s nice to be able to attach business meaning to your measures, as multiple metrics often share similar names. In our banking model alone, total_trans_amount , settled_volume , and unsettled_volume could all casually be called "volume" by a business user. That ambiguity can trip up both analysts building reports and AI agents translating natural-language prompts into SQL. With the GA, you can embed rich semantic metadata directly into each measure definition using the OPTIONS clause, including plain-language description strings, domain synonyms, and custom key-value extensions: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "-- Business meaning and governance metadata travel with the metric
MEASURE(SUM(CASE WHEN is_settled = TRUE THEN amount ELSE 0.0 END)) 
 AS settled_volume
 OPTIONS (
 description = 'Transaction value that settled. Excludes fees.',
 synonyms = ['settled amount', 'cleared volume'],
 extensions = [('unit', 'USD'),
 ('owner', 'finance-analytics'),
 ('reporting_tier', 'executive')]
 )"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c3d2c690>)])]> Because this business context lives inside the schema alongside the SQL formula, your semantic definitions travel wherever the metric is queried. Make measures discoverable to humans and AI agents BigQuery directly integrates with Knowledge Catalog to create a unified discovery and consumption loop for both people and machines: Enterprise-wide context discovery in Knowledge Catalog: BigQuery Graph and measures metadata is automatically ingested and searchable in Knowledge Catalog as a native resource alongside tables, views, and routines. Data stewards, analysts, and AI agents can search across the catalog using business synonyms or descriptions, inspect governance tags, and view the underlying measure’s SQL definitions (such as SUM(CASE WHEN is_settled = TRUE...) ) to verify how each metric is calculated before using it. In Knowledge Catalog, you can also enrich graph metadata with business glossaries and stewardship context, uniting asset discovery, business meaning, and mathematical measures in a single pane so users and agents can work from the same context. Runtime schema introspection in BigQuery: Calling BQ.SHOW_GRAPH_EXPAND_SCHEMA returns an expanded graph's schema as JSON without scanning underlying tables, flagging metrics with "is_measure": true alongside their descriptions and synonyms. Passing flatten_results => FALSE preserves your entity hierarchy as nested ROW ( STRUCT ) types, letting agents inspect the relational tree and query paths like Account.District.city directly. Connect across your data and AI ecosystem Finally, BigQuery measures integrates across the Google Cloud data and AI stack so you can author, reuse, and query semantics in the tools you already use: Author with AI: Use the graph skills in Data Agent Kit to scaffold, author, and validate BigQuery measure definitions using natural-language prompts in your preferred AI coding environment. Reuse existing LookML models: If you already model business metrics in Looker, you can model once using LookML-based derived analytic models to compile Explores, joins, and measures directly into native BigQuery Graph models. Query with natural language: Unified graph and measure definitions are supported out-of-the-box in Conversational Analytics , enabling business users and AI agents to ask complex questions against governed metrics in plain natural language. Get started with BigQuery measures The primary advantage of this unified model is that you can build from the foundation you already have. If you already run a BI semantic layer, take a governed metric and define it directly on the entity it describes; if your foundation is a knowledge graph, attach a unified measure to your most frequent traversal. Whichever side you start from, you are building a single source of truth for both your BI dashboards and your AI agents. To see unified semantics in action, watch the BigQuery measures introduction video , or dive into the BigQuery measures documentation and BigQuery Graph overview . When you are ready to build hands-on, try our step-by-step codelabs for music streaming analytics .

The what is a governed metric, like revenue at risk; the why is the network of relationships that produced it. title: Experimenting with ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE
raw_text:
Standard Network Policies limit you to applying policies at the namespace level, but ClusterNetworkPolicy (CNP) lets you apply granular networking policies across an entire cluster. When you use CNP, you can easily scale security and governance policies. Recently, I experimented with this functionality in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and saw the benefits for myself. In this post, we'll explore using CNP to control traffic to an LLM and cluster. If you want to jump right into a hands-on lab, check out this Codelab: Secure AI Inference Workloads with GKE ClusterNetworkPolicy . How CNP works CNP follows a three-tier flow with a precedence match: Admin tier (top precedence) : Cluster administrator enforces mandatory security rules that can't be bypassed (for example, blocking metadata access). Network policy tier (middle precedence) : Standard namespace-scoped policies that are managed by application teams to control ingress and egress for their microservices. Baseline tier (bottom precedence) : Cluster administrator establishes fallback defaults (for example, a default-deny posture across namespaces). Design pattern example The aim of the experiment in the Codelab is to restrict traffic to the LLM namespace, allow only authorized clients, and prevent cluster-wide access to the metadata API except for DNS port 53. It uses these services: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) : Provides private networking, subnets for pods and services, and secure outbound egress via Cloud NAT. TPU v5e : High-efficiency accelerator hardware (2x2 topology) running optimized model inference. GKE : Managed Kubernetes platform that's powered by GKE Dataplane V2 (eBPF) to enforce multi-tier networking policies. Gemma 4 ( google/gemma-4-E2B-it ) : Lightweight open model served with vLLM to act as a sensitive AI workload. ClusterNetworkPolicy (CNP) : Cluster-wide policies that let administrators enforce mandatory administrator and baseline guardrails across all namespaces. NetworkPolicies : Standard namespace-scoped rules that let developers grant access to authorized clients. Cloud Logging / GKE Network Policy Logging : Captures real-time packet verdicts ( allow / deny ) and policy audit trails. Putting it together: Setup overview Setting up this environment begins with building a custom private network infrastructure and deploying your TPU-enabled clusters: Custom VPC & Cloud NAT : Establish a custom VPC with a dedicated subnet that hosts primary nodes, plus secondary CIDR IP address ranges for GKE pods ( 10.20.0.0/16 ) and services ( 10.30.0.0/20 ). A Cloud Router and Cloud NAT are configured to handle secure outbound egress for nodes while blocking inbound internet exposure. GKE Standard cluster : Spin up a Standard GKE cluster running GKE Dataplane V2 ( ADVANCED_DATAPATH ). GKE Dataplane V2 acts as the core engine that leverages eBPF under the hood to enforce both standard and cluster-scoped policies dynamically. Dedicated TPU v5e node pool : Provision a node pool featuring ct5lp-hightpu-4t machines arranged in a 2x2 topology slice. The nodes carry a dedicated taint ( google.com/tpu=present:NoSchedule ) to ensure that only accelerator workloads run on them. Deploying the Gemma 4 workload : Isolate the pods by creating three distinct namespaces: gemma-llm ( tier: ai-core ): Serves the lightweight Gemma 4 model using the high-performance vllm/vllm-tpu:latest engine on port 8000. client-ns ( tier: app-frontend ): Runs the authorized chat client that must query the model. untrusted-tenant ( tier: untrusted ): Represents an unauthorized probe container simulating a rogue client. Securing the LLM and metadata: Code walkthrough By default in Kubernetes, all cross-namespace and egress traffic is open. To enforce a defense-in-depth posture, we apply network policies across the GKE evaluation tiers. Step 1: Establish zero-trust posture (baseline tier) To deny all unauthorized ingress cluster-wide, the cluster administrator applies a ClusterNetworkPolicy at the baseline tier. This tier acts as a fallback safety net. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'apiVersion: policy.networking.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: ClusterNetworkPolicy
metadata:
 name: baseline-default-deny
spec:
 tier: Baseline
 priority: 1000
 subject:
 namespaces: {}
 ingress:
 - name: allow-dns-ingress
 action: Accept
 from:
 - namespaces: {}
 protocols:
 - udp:
 destinationPort:
 number: 53
 - tcp:
 destinationPort:
 number: 53
 - name: baseline-deny-cross-ns
 action: Deny
 from:
 - namespaces: {}'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36cde68c10>)])]> How it works Precedence placement : Setting tier: Baseline places this policy at the very bottom of the GKE evaluation chain, and the priority: 1000 value orders it within that tier. It only processes traffic that hasn't matched a rule in any higher tier. Global target : Specifying subject.namespaces: {} ensures that this fallback applies globally to every pod in every namespace. DNS isolation exemption : The first ingress rule accepts incoming DNS traffic on TCP and UDP port 53. Without this explicit exemption, cluster-wide DNS resolution would fail. Fallback deny : The second rule matches any incoming pod-to-pod connection attempt and drops it. At this stage, both the client-ns and untrusted-tenant namespaces are blocked from contacting Gemma. Step 2: Delegate access to developers (networkpolicy tier) With the baseline default-deny active, the application team that manages gemma-llm can safely delegate access to legitimate clients. They define a standard namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy to allow incoming port 8000 traffic from rag-agent pods in the client-ns namespace. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
 name: allow-rag-client
 namespace: gemma-llm
spec:
 podSelector:
 matchLabels:
 app: gemma-service
 policyTypes:
 - Ingress
 ingress:
 # Explicitly permit ingress only from pods matching app: rag-agent in client-ns
 - from:
 - namespaceSelector:
 matchLabels:
 kubernetes.io/metadata.name: client-ns
 podSelector:
 matchLabels:
 app: rag-agent
 ports:
 - protocol: TCP
 port: 8000'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c390ed10>)])]> How it works Developer control : This resource resides within the gemma-llm namespace and it's managed directly by the developer, matching the GKE focus on operational separation. Middle precedence matching : Standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicies map directly to the NetworkPolicy Tier. Because this tier is evaluated before the baseline tier, incoming TCP packets from the authorized client to port 8000 match this rule and are immediately accepted. Fall-through block : Connections that originate from the untrusted-tenant namespace fail to match this rule, pass through to the baseline tier, and are dropped. Step 3: Enforce global egress guardrails (admin tier) By default, Pods can query the GKE link-local Compute Engine metadata server ( 169.254.169.254 ). Those queries expose instance metadata and potentially high-privilege service account tokens. To lock this down, the cluster administrator applies an egress guardrail at the highest tier in the GKE hierarchy. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'apiVersion: policy.networking.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: ClusterNetworkPolicy
metadata:
 name: admin-global-guardrails
spec:
 tier: Admin
 priority: 10
 subject:
 namespaces: {} # Targets every namespace in the cluster
 ingress:
 # Delegate all ingress decisions down to developer and baseline tiers
 - name: delegate-all-ingress
 action: Pass
 from:
 - namespaces: {}
 egress:
 # Allow DNS resolution so pods can locate endpoints
 - name: allow-all-dns
 action: Accept
 to:
 - networks:
 - 0.0.0.0/0
 protocols:
 - udp:
 destinationPort:
 number: 53
 - tcp:
 destinationPort:
 number: 53
 # Hard deny on the Compute Engine metadata server
 - name: block-metadata-server-global
 action: Deny
 to:
 - networks:
 - 169.254.169.254/32
 # Delegate remaining egress traffic to lower tiers
 - name: delegate-other-egress
 action: Pass
 to:
 - namespaces: {}'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36c390ee50>)])]> How it works Admin tier precedence : Deploying this policy in the admin tier ensures that it's evaluated first, and priority 10 orders it within that tier. GKE processes this policy before standard NetworkPolicies and baseline rules. Controlled delegation : The delegate-all-ingress and delegate-other-egress rules have an action: Pass directive that instructs the engine to forward evaluation down to the next tier for remaining in-cluster traffic. Inviolable guardrail : When any pod attempts to query 169.254.169.254/32 on non-DNS ports, the query matches the block-metadata-server-global rule and it's dropped. Because this drop occurs at the top admin tier, it can't be bypassed or overridden, even if a namespace developer deploys an allow-all egress policy. Verifying with Observability for GKE Verifying and auditing security policies is straightforward using the built-in telemetry capabilities of GKE Dataplane V2: Hubble eBPF streams : Provides real-time, kernel-level packet inspection without injecting sidecars. Administrators can stream live network flows to observe policy verdicts as they happen, making it easy to validate allowed communication paths and identify dropped packets immediately. GKE Network Logging and Cloud Logging : Automatically exports structured connection telemetry and policy enforcement verdicts directly into Cloud Logging. Teams can filter and alert on policy decisions using attributes such as disposition="deny" , source/destination namespaces, and jsonPayload.policies[0].name to maintain audit compliance and investigate blocked connection attempts. CNP can be useful and, as always, when you use it in your production environment, you'll need to plan and design the rules based on your setup. Next steps Take a deeper dive and find more information on these features: ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE: Balancing control and autonomy for your microservices Configuring GKE ClusterNetworkPolicy Want to ask a question, find out more, or share a thought? Connect with me on LinkedIn !
summary: Standard Network Policies limit you to applying policies at the namespace level, but ClusterNetworkPolicy (CNP) lets you apply granular networking policies across an entire cluster. When you use CNP, you can easily scale security and governance policies. Recently, I experimented with this functionality in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and saw the benefits for myself. In this post, we'll explore using CNP to control traffic to an LLM and cluster.

title: The Blueprint: How Authentic Brands Group expands creativity with AuthOS
raw_text: Welcome to The Blueprint, a new feature where we highlight how Google Cloud customers are tackling unique and common challenges across industries using the latest AI and cloud technologies. We hope to inspire others looking to innovate in their work. Authentic Brands Group, a global lifestyle and entertainment platform, is the owner of some of the most iconic intellectual property and cultural assets in the world. Authentic’s portfolio spans more than 50 brands, from Reebok and Juicy Couture to Shaquille O’Neal and Elvis Presley, and reaches nearly one billion social media followers.The company accelerates its brands through a set of specialized businesses that combine powerful storytelling, premium content, unforgettable live experiences and global commerce. The challenge: Authentic’s platform requires a highly efficient exchange of information and deep coordination between its specialized business units, including entertainment, creative, marketing, live events, business development and more. The platform also requires ongoing communication and coordination with Authentic’s more than 1,700 licensees and strategic partners worldwide. These demands are deeply interconnected: Marketing needs to deliver fast, brand-specific creative assets; creative teams must visualize new concepts in minutes, not weeks, and business development must research and prepare compelling proposals for potential partners. These teams work together to accelerate brand growth across categories and geographies. As the Authentic platform has grown, moving beyond traditional, siloed tools became essential to staying competitive. Authentic needed an enterprise AI operating system that could support each brand’s unique voice and visual identity, provide instant access to proprietary business data, and help teams move faster without sacrificing quality or consistency. aside_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('title', "AI that's really Authentic"), ('body', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36ce6e0f10>), ('btn_text', 'Read it now.'), ('href', 'https://cloud.google.com/transform/authentic-brands-group-auth-ai-gemini-innovation-across-brands/'), ('image', <GAEImage: ABG-AOS-hero-final>)])]> The solution: To tackle this challenge, Authentic built AuthOS, an AI operating system powered by Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and Cloud Run. Its 50 interconnected AI agents and tools help teams create compelling content faster, streamline workflows, and reduce time spent across disconnected tools. AuthOS augments Google Cloud's large language models with unique Authentic brand and partner context and enterprise data stores. This allows teams to analyze business needs, brand knowledge and market intelligence to generate more relevant forecasts and recommendations. For example, the Video Generator agent's multimodel pipeline utilizes Gemini 3.1 Flash and Gemini Omni to create cinematic starting and ending frames, Vision AI for detailed visual analysis, Gemini 3 for prompt optimization, and Veo 3.1 for final video generation. Together, these tools help maintain visual consistency and fidelity to each brand’s identity. The Architecture: The Outcome: After launching our AI operating system we quickly saw how Vertex AI supported our AI workflow experimentation and iteration. We’re now able to incorporate any of the hundreds of models we want from Model Garden. More than 80% of employees are using AuthOS weekly. We're thrilled with how the platform is benefiting our business, and are seeing tangible results. For example, AI-enhanced product images for Reebok, our largest brand, delivered more than 60% higher return on ad spend (ROAS) compared to unenhanced imagery. AuthOS is also democratizing content production. Now, creative departments are joined by business development quickly creating pitch materials and marketing coordinators testing concepts without investing in full production. Perhaps most important of all, Vertex AI's modular architecture makes it possible for Authentic to keep up with the ever-evolving AI landscape by integrating new tools almost immediately. These capabilities give employees across Authentic new ways to create, collaborate and accelerate the growth of its brands worldwide. title: Introducing Gemini for healthcare
raw_text: Every healthcare organization is working to deliver great care to more people at a lower cost. However, a general AI model is not enough to solve this challenge. Today, healthcare runs on fragmented data. Patient records, coverage policies, and clinical evidence remain trapped across disconnected records, claims systems, and administrative tools that don’t work together. Clinicians are forced to spend nearly 28 hours a week on manually reconciling information, and patients wait for answers about their care and their coverage. Healthcare organizations need a single, secure, governed orchestration layer that coordinates work across the systems they already run, assembling verifiable evidence and taking multi-step workflows through to completion with human oversight. Today, we are announcing Gemini for healthcare . This purpose-built industry solution extends the universal Gemini agent , we introduced last month at Gemini at Work. The Gemini agent is a single, always-on agent for work where employees delegate an objective, and the agent plans the steps, retains organizational context, and routes across the best models to deliver finished outcomes inside the tools teams already use. The Gemini agent is built with enterprise-grade identity administration, fine-grained access control, and centralized policy management directly into its runtime. Every agent operates with a distinct identity, inherits each user’s existing role-based permissions, and enforces strict need-to-know boundaries across every user, sub-agent, and workflow . Working across clinical, financial, and administrative systems, it orchestrates multi-step tasks without forcing teams to switch applications: For providers: Gemini provides a patient’s history across care settings, charts are prepared before the visit, and authorization packets are assembled against payer policy before submission, so fewer claims come back denied. For health plans and payers: Gemini ensures requests are checked against medical policy and organized for the clinical reviewer, and benefits and costs are explained to members from their own plan documents. Gemini for healthcare is built to support HIPAA compliance, with governance running underneath it all. It’s available starting today in preview. Gemini for healthcare Gemini for healthcare empowers payers and providers to orchestrate complex clinical, operational, and administrative workflows. Four components of Gemini for healthcare Developed alongside clinical and health plan leaders, Gemini for healthcare provides an integrated, fully governed environment configured for payers and providers with four core components: Skills for healthcare work: Skills are reusable instructions and context, written by domain experts, that teach Gemini to run a specific task. Purpose-built, multi-step instructions guide the Gemini agent through essential clinical and administrative tasks, such as medical records synthesis, pre-appointment preparation, coverage and policy review, and payer benefit determination. Each skill applies your organization’s policies and plan rules, and teams can build custom skills tailored to the workflows and standard operating procedures unique to their organization. Connectors to clinical, financial, and operational systems: A library of connectors links Gemini directly to the EHR, claims, care management, and administrative systems organizations already run. Gemini queries each system while strictly preserving existing identity and role-based access controls, so teams get unified context without migrating sensitive data or altering permissions. An open healthcare partner ecosystem: Every health system and health plan runs a different mix of systems. Healthcare systems integrators and digital health partners help organizations extend Gemini with specialized solutions, connect it to what they already run, and scale it without lock-in. A secure, governed platform with open model choice: Clinical, security, and IT leaders get one place to set and enforce policies that govern every agent interaction. It is built to support HIPAA compliance, with enterprise-grade access controls, end-to-end audit logging, and verifiable citations so reviewers can check where each answer came from. Because the agent supports model choice, organizations can pair frontier models from Google and leading partners for complex clinical reasoning with fast, cost-efficient models for routine administrative steps under the same governance. Unlocking high-value workflows with skills designed for payers and providers Gemini for healthcare takes on the heavy assembly and administrative work that slows down clinical decisions and coverage determinations. At the point of care: Building a longitudinal timeline from fragmented sources: Synthesizes EHR and external records, separates active problems from resolved ones, lists allergies, and flags medication discrepancies. Clinicians get a grounded and unified patient picture in minutes rather than piecing together history across disconnected systems. Reclaiming preparation time between patients: Prepares the patient chart ahead of a scheduled visit or procedure, flagging interval events, current medications, and outstanding clearances, labs, or consents, so care teams walk in with the full picture. Streamlining clinical authorization and appeals: Extracts relevant chart evidence into an audit-ready packet for review, aligned with payer policy, flagging documentation gaps before submission rather than after a denial. If denials do occur, and the record supports it, it drafts an appeal grounded directly in the clinical record and the plan’s policy. At the point of coverage: Accelerating payer review: Checks incoming requests against the health plan’s medical policies and organizes the findings for reviewers, with findings traceable to the submitted documentation and coverage policy. Clinical reviewers spend less time assembling files and more time applying professional judgment. Demystifying benefits and patient financial liability: Parses complex plan benefit booklets to estimate out-of-pocket costs, track deductibles, and verify in-network status, giving member services staff a step-by-step breakdown grounded in the member’s actual plan documents. For Medicare Advantage members, it applies Medicare’s coverage criteria where a plan’s internal rule is stricter. Open ecosystem of connectors across the healthcare tech stack Gemini for healthcare connects directly to core clinical, operational, and industry systems via secure connectors , inheriting each source system’s existing role-based access controls and data permissions. EHRs and clinical data integration: Epic EHR : Gives authorized users read-only access to patient conditions, medications, labs, clinical notes, and specialist documentation. With no write-back to the underlying chart, clinical data integrity remains completely intact. Oracle Health EHR: Surfaces read-only patient histories, diagnostics, lab results, and clinical documentation for authorized users while enforcing zero write-back to ensure data integrity for the system of record. InterSystems FHIR Server : Extending beyond EHR integrations, InterSystems FHIR MCP Server provides standardized, high-performance FHIR repository management and clinical data interoperability. Verato : Resolves patient identity and matches records across visits and sources. Keragon - Healthcare Integrations : Provides connectivity to 400+ healthcare applications, including EHRs, enabling organizations to securely connect their existing healthcare systems through a single MCP integration. Eligibility, claims, and pricing: Optum Coordination of Benefits : Finds additional patient coverage and determines the correct order of benefits before billing. Currently in limited release and testing with Gemini for Healthcare. Optum Network Eligibility : Retrieves patient eligibility and benefit details from connected health plans in real time. Currently in limited release and testing with Gemini for Healthcare. TriZetto Provider Solutions: Verifies patient eligibility, coverage, co-pays, and deductibles across Medicare, Medicaid, and major commercial plans via TriZetto's vast network. GoodRx : Enables care teams to discover prescription pricing and savings options, including manufacturer-sponsored self-pay programs, directly within AI-powered workflows to help patients access more affordable medications. Infinitus Relay : Automates high-volume payer phone calls required for prior authorization and benefit verification. Terminology and coding: IMO Health : Brings terminology normalization, clinical search, and knowledge graphs into healthcare skills and governed agentic workflows. ICD-10 Codes : Searches and validates ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes, billable status, and hierarchy. RxNorm Drug Vocabulary : Looks up standardized drug names, ingredients, strengths, dose forms, and NDCs. Coverage and provider reference: CMS Coverage : Connects directly to Medicare coverage rules, National and Local Coverage Determinations (NCDs/LCDs), ensuring coverage reasoning rests on current published policy rather than static model knowledge. NPPES NPI Registry : Verifies provider identity, clinical taxonomy, and practice location in real time. Evidence based guidelines: Optum EvidenceVue: Turns real-world clinical data into actionable evidence through AI-powered workflows from Optum Life Sciences. BMJ Digital Health: Delivers expert-curated, structured, peer-reviewed clinical guidelines and evidence, grounding care and coverage decisions in verifiable citations. Clinical and operational workflows: Salesforce : Headless Salesforce Health Cloud integrations bring workflows, data models, and Agentforce into Gemini for governed action right in the flow of work. Suki : Delivers Ambient Clinical Intelligence across healthcare workflows, transforming clinical conversations into actionable intelligence that powers documentation, coding, revenue cycle management, and clinical reasoning. UiPath : Connects healthcare-ready UiPath automations and agents to help teams assemble citation-backed context for operational reviews, prior authorizations, and appeals. Synthpop Careflow: Orchestrates the patient journey across referral intake, coverage verification, and patient follow-up, turning unstructured referrals into validated, payer-ready orders without manual re-entry. Alteryx : Enables healthcare teams to turn their domain expertise into automated analytics workflows, grounding AI-driven insights in business rules and calculations that are visible, understandable, repeatable, and auditable. Enterprise productivity and collaboration: Sana from Workday: Connects HR, finance, and enterprise knowledge so healthcare teams can surface policies, coordinate tasks, and get work done across administrative systems. ServiceNow : Tracks IT incidents, operational service requests, and approval chains while enforcing existing enterprise routing rules. Microsoft 365 : Integrates directly with Word, Outlook, and SharePoint so prepared authorization packets, appeal letters, and benefit breakdowns land directly in the tools where teams already work. Google Workspace : Connects seamlessly with Google Docs, Gmail, Drive, and Sheets to surface internal files and coordinate administrative workflows while enforcing enterprise access controls. Security and compliance: Cyera Dataport : Integrates with Cyera for data and agent security, delivering protected health information (PHI) context to support HIPAA audits and compliance reporting. Global implementation partners and ecosystem Through our open platform, organizations can deploy specialized partner agents such as ASCO Oncology Guideline Assistant or work with healthcare systems integrators, including 66degrees, Accenture, Altimetrik, AuxoAI, Cognizant, Deloitte, Egen, HCLTech, KPMG, NTT DATA, PwC, Quantiphi, Slalom, Tata Consultancy Services, TEKsystems Global Services, and Wipro, to customize, integrate, and scale these capabilities across complex enterprise architectures without vendor lock-in. Healthcare video Optum Insight shares how Gemini for healthcare brings value to healthcare professionals at every stage. Developed alongside leading healthcare organizations Health systems, health plan providers, academic medical centers, and clinical leaders are already working with Google Cloud to shape and apply these capabilities across care delivery, plan operations, and medical research: Synthesizing patient context at the point of care “Making it easier for physicians to access and understand a patient’s medical history helps them spend less time gathering information and more time focused on patient care. Through our work with Google Cloud, we’re exploring how Gemini can interpret and synthesize complex patient information from multiple electronic health record systems and care settings, connecting data from different sources to give clinicians a more complete and cohesive understanding of a patient’s medical history.” — Michael J. Schlosser, MD, MBA, FAANS, Executive Vice President and Chief Clinical Officer, HCA Healthcare. “Healthcare generates enormous amounts of information and data every day, yet patients often experience care as a series of separate interactions rather than one connected journey. Through our work with Google Cloud, we're exploring how AI can help connect information across the healthcare experience, making it easier to support the whole person, create more personalized care experiences, and equip clinicians with meaningful insights at the right time.” — Karen Hanlon, President, Highmark Health. "By leveraging Gemini for healthcare, we will be able to use technology in a way that elevates the patient experience and strengthens the relationship between caregivers and those they serve. Through these integrated solutions, we expect to ease some of the administrative burden on our clinical teams and give them more time for what matters most: caring for their patients. Technology is at its best when it supports our caregivers and strengthens the human connection that is at the heart of healthcare." — Dr. John D'Angelo, President and CEO, Northwell Health . Streamlining coverage, benefits, and payer operations “ The real promise of AI in healthcare isn’t simply doing today’s work faster. It’s creating a better way for the health system to work. When payers and providers can connect data, insights and workflows more seamlessly, we can remove unnecessary complexity, improve performance and help the entire system work better .” — Sandeep Dadlani, Chief Executive Officer, Optum Insight . “Gemini for healthcare serves as a foundation for our unified architecture of reusable AI agents, enabling us to deliver new capabilities and productivity gains significantly faster than traditional development cycles. Our focus going forward is an agentic-AI model, where an intelligence layer drives deeper automation and operational transformation. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is working toward that future in healthcare with Google Cloud." — Prem Somasundaram, Chief Information Officer, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts. Accelerating clinical research and evidence-based guidelines “For oncology care providers, quick access to current and relevant information is not a luxury, but a necessity. We are excited about what Gemini for healthcare could do to help care providers quickly find the critical information they need, when they need it, so they can drive better outcomes for patients.” — Clifford Hudis, MD, FACP, FASCO, Chief Executive Officer, American Society of Clinical Oncology. Built on an enterprise-grade foundation Google is both a frontier AI lab and an enterprise cloud. Gemini for healthcare runs on Google Cloud’s secure infrastructure and is built to support HIPAA compliance . Clinical data, prompts, and generated outputs remain within your organization’s governed environment and are never used to train or fine-tune Google’s foundation models. Outputs are grounded in clinical records, plan policies, and your organization’s approved guidelines and evidence, with traceable citations and audit logging that give clinical, compliance, and IT leaders visibility and control. And because we operate the full stack, from infrastructure and models through security and the application layer, we can optimize performance, reliability, and cost together, routing high-volume administrative tasks to fast, low-cost models and reserving high-reasoning models for complex clinical and operational analysis, so organizations can scale AI across the enterprise without scaling spend at the same rate. This is just the beginning The launch of Gemini for healthcare marks another step in our commitment to bring the best of Gemini to every professional and every workflow, natively tailored to the way their industry works. Gemini for healthcare is available in preview in the U.S. today, joining our expanding suite of purpose-built solutions for legal , financial services , and government services . We invite leaders across health systems, medical groups, health plan providers, and payers to explore how Gemini can transform their most critical clinical and operational workflows.

title: The open AI-native stack on Kubernetes: From open models to distributed inference and agents
raw_text:
Over the past decade, Kubernetes established itself as the standard for orchestrating microservices and containerized applications. Today, we're witnessing the next major architectural shift in distributed computing: AI workloads moving from isolated research prototypes into large-scale, multi-tenant production fleets . In this post, we'll walk through the open-source stack that powers this shift and show you the sample manifests that you can try on your own Kubernetes clusters. You can also join us at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 to see these projects in action through live demos and technical sessions. For modern engineering teams, production AI is rapidly moving beyond generic calls to closed, black-box APIs. Organizations are realizing that their long-term competitive advantage lies in domain specialization. Platform engineers, ML researchers, and AI builders want the autonomy to run high-performing open-weight models (such as the Gemma family). They want to adapt them to proprietary enterprise datasets by using reinforcement learning (RL) and serve them with predictable latency, high throughput, and maximum hardware efficiency. Whether it's scientific initiatives training domain models like DolphinGemma (an LLM helping scientists study how dolphins communicate) on acoustic data, legal platforms evaluating complex contracts, or engineering teams building autonomous coding agents, the objective is the same: achieving frontier-level task performance at a fraction of the serving cost and latency. Yet, scaling RL post-training, stateful distributed inference, and autonomous agent execution on traditional container infrastructure introduces substantial hurdles: Accelerator underutilization in RL : When you alternate between training and rollout generation, expensive GPUs and TPUs remain idle for most of the training run. Cache-blind load balancing : When you use standard Kubernetes round-robin and least-connections routing, multi-turn agent calls are scattered across arbitrary pods and wipe out key-value (KV) cache locality. Framework fragmentation : When you operate parallel, siloed compute clusters (such as bespoke Ray or Slurm setups) alongside Kubernetes, you fragment capacity and multiply maintenance toil. Agent security in multi-tenant clusters: When you execute untrusted, model-generated shell commands and scripts in shared environments, you expose clusters to sandbox escapes and privilege escalation. At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 , Google Cloud is addressing these challenges by introducing and expanding a unified, open-source AI-native stack across Kubernetes and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) based on these components: OpenRL (CNCF Sandbox): A Kubernetes-native post training service that simplifies RL post-training and maximizes accelerator utilization. llm-d 1.0 (CNCF Sandbox): An open distributed inference control plane that provides prefix-cache-aware routing, disaggregated serving, and multi-tier KV cache management. Ray on GKE with KubeRay (CNCF Sandbox) : A framework that provides enterprise lifecycle management, elastic autoscaling, and Kueue -driven scheduling for distributed Ray compute and data processing. Agent Substrate (CNCF Sandbox) : An open orchestration runtime that provides lifecycle management and execution targets for multi-turn AI agent workflows. gVisor (CNCF Sandbox) : A kernel-level container sandbox that delivers strong system call isolation when you execute untrusted agent code in multi-tenant clusters. TorchTPU : A backend that provides first-class, native PyTorch support across Cloud TPUs and GPUs inside upstream vLLM and SGLang . Bridge reinforcement learning and Kubernetes with OpenRL While supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become standard practice, domain excellence especially in multi-step reasoning, mathematical proofing, and autonomous tool use requires RL. Historically, it's been difficult to bridge the world of ML experimentation with production Kubernetes fleets. ML researchers want to iterate rapidly in Python and PyTorch by using standard reward functions, while platform teams need multi-tenant governance, quota enforcement, and predictable scheduling. To eliminate this friction, Google created OpenRL and contributed it to the CNCF Sandbox . Architectural highlights of OpenRL Clean 4-primitive Python abstraction : Researchers write standard Python training code that's centered around four core primitives ( forward_backward , optim_step , sample , and save_state ). OpenRL translates these primitives into Kubernetes scheduling workflows without requiring developers to learn Kubernetes internals or manage infrastructure code. Cooperative accelerator time-slicing : OpenRL interleaves training steps and rollout inferences on the same physical accelerators. This approach avoids the need to dedicate separate, static clusters to compute-bound training and latency-sensitive rollout generation. Delta-weight synchronization : Shipping full multi-gigabyte model weights over cluster networking after every optimization step creates massive network saturation. OpenRL transmits only parameter deltas to rollout workers, eliminating rollout cold starts. Zero-config dynamic resource allocation ( DRA ) : OpenRL automatically profiles model context lengths, batch dimensions, and LoRA versus full fine-tuning configurations. It then dynamically bin-packs workloads across a heterogenous accelerator fleet by using native Kubernetes DRA claims. Distributed inference at scale with llm-d 1.0 After you post-train a model, serving it serving it under interactive, bursty agent traffic presents a new set of distributed systems challenges. Standard ingress controllers treat LLM traffic as stateless HTTP requests, scattering sequential turns across different replicas and constantly rebuilding KV cache. Google Cloud, Red Hat, IBM Research, CoreWeave, and NVIDIA co-founded the project, with contributions from over 500 engineers across 25+ organizations. Today, llm-d 1.0 is the CNCF Sandbox distributed inference control plane that transforms standalone inference engines (like vLLM and SGLang) into a coordinated, cluster-wide serving fabric. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'apiVersion: inference.networking.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: InferencePool
metadata:
 name: gemma-serving-pool
 namespace: ai-serving
spec:
 targetRef:
 group: apps
 kind: Deployment
 name: vllm-gemma-27b
 scheduling:
 # Routes multi-turn requests to replicas holding matching KV context
 strategy: PrefixCacheAware
 fallback: LeastQueueDepth
 observability:
 kvCacheSyncInterval: "50ms"'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f36cfef0550>)])]> Core capabilities of llm-d 1.0 Prefix-cache-aware routing ( Endpoint Picker ) : The Endpoint Picker integrates into the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension, and GKE manages it natively through GKE Inference Gateway . The Endpoint Picker evaluates real-time KV cache residency across worker pods. In production deployments, it's doubled KV cache hit rates from 35% to 70% and cut median time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 70-85% on multi-turn agent workloads. 3-Tier KV cache offload : When accelerator high-bandwidth memory (HBM) nears capacity during long-context interactions, llm-d cascades KV cache blocks from HBM → host CPU RAM → local NVMe SSD / Google Cloud Managed Lustre / Cloud Storage. This offload prevents expensive context recalculations. EPD Disaggregation with DisaggregatedSet : Decouples Encoding, Prefill, and Decode (EPD) onto specialized hardware pools that are connected by high-speed interconnects. DisaggregatedSet is built built on Kubernetes LeaderWorkerSet (LWS) . It enables independent horizontal scaling and coordinated, zero-downtime rolling upgrades. Native TorchTPU upstream support : PyTorch models run natively on Google Cloud TPUs inside upstream vLLM and SGLang through TorchTPU. Developers get day-zero parity across TPU v5e, v6e, and v7x alongside NVIDIA GPUs without the need to maintain private forks or rewrite pipelines. Latency-tolerant async processing & flow control : The llm-d-async-processor component pulls background, latency-tolerant tasks from Pub/Sub or Redis into cluster slack capacity. It applies strict traffic prioritization so background processing never degrades interactive user experiences. Fleet observability with Prism : Track cluster-wide throughput, inter-token latency (ITL), TTFT, and cache hit ratios by using Prism , the llm-d open-source benchmarking and performance dashboard. Distributed Python & ML orchestration with KubeRay While specialized runtimes handle inference and RL loops, distributed data preparation, embedding generation, and distributed PyTorch training depend heavily on Ray . KubeRay provides an open-source, Kubernetes-native operator that manages the complete lifecycle of Ray clusters, jobs, and services ( RayCluster , RayJob , and RayService custom resources) on Kubernetes. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'apiVersion: ray.io/v1

 - transformers==4.40.0

 - groupName: gpu-workers

Native Kueue queueing & multi-tenancy : KubeRay integrates directly with Kueue for multi-tenant fair sharing, priority preemption, and quota management across shared GPU and TPU capacity. Elastic autoscaling : KubeRay dynamically scales worker pods based on active Ray tasks and actor placement, preventing idle resource consumption. Strong isolation for AI agents: Agent Substrate & gVisor As multi-turn AI agents advance from conversational assistants to autonomous systems that generate code, execute shell commands, and orchestrate external APIs running untrusted, model-generated code in shared clusters introduces serious security risks. Google Cloud is contributing Agent Substrate and continuing core contributions to gVisor in the CNCF Sandbox: Kernel-level sandboxing : gVisor provides a user-space kernel that intercepts and virtualizes system calls, which helps ensure that untrusted agent code can't compromise the host kernel or access neighboring tenant workloads. Sub-second ephemeral execution : Sandboxes spin up in milliseconds per agent turn, providing isolated execution environments for both RL rollout generation in OpenRL and live production agent workflows. Proven in practice: Mastering domain reasoning To evaluate this complete open-source stack on a rigorous enterprise workload, we tested Gemma 4 against the open-source Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) developed by Harvey.ai . This benchmark spans 24 complex legal practice areas from mergers and acquisitions (M&A)M&A due diligence to contract dispute analysis. The evaluation produced these results: Benchmark results : While standard SFT plateaued around 50% accuracy on multi-step reasoning rubrics, when we applied reproducible RL loops with OpenRL, we lifted model accuracy to 70% . Operational efficiency : The entire training pipeline dynamically shared GPU and TPU capacity with concurrent LoRA and inference jobs on GKE without manual partition management. How teams are adopting this stack Organization persona Core challenge Architecture with OpenRL + llm-d + KubeRay + Gemma Enterprise platform teams Manage multiple internal ML squads without fragmented Slurm/Ray clusters or runaway hardware bills. Transform existing GKE clusters into self-hosted Reinforcement Learning-as-a-Service (RLaaS) by using DRA, Kueue, and accelerator time-slicing. Regulated enterprises (finance, healthcare, legal) Intellectual property (IP), compliance, and privacy mandates prohibit sending proprietary data to third-party public APIs. Post-train and serve 1B-30B Gemma models completely inside a private Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with domain-specific reward functions for superior task accuracy and lower total cost of ownership (TCO). AI-native builders & agent developers High serving costs and latency bottlenecks on long-context, multi-turn agent interactions. Deploy llm-d prefix-cache routing that's paired with gVisor-isolated Agent Sandbox execution targets. Model-as-a-Service & neocloud providers Deliver high-margin, multi-tenant post-training and inference across diverse hardware fleets.
